About this printable

9 printable tools for ages 2–5: picture checklists, together tokens, helping jobs, a family plan and a 30-day tracker.

The Play-First Family Kit for ages 2–5 has 9 printable tools, in a PDF you can type in: picture checklists, tokens, helping jobs and a family plan. It gives your day a kind shape: jobs first, then play and time together, then screens at their usual spot. Nothing is taken away; there’s just more play.

The Play First, Then Screens checklist comes with big pictures for ages 2–5 and as a fillable blank. Each has 4 colorways and a Monday or Sunday start. Little ones also get a helping-jobs chart and a first-then-later Play-First Board.

The whole family gets 24 together tokens (12 ready-made, 12 blank) and six screen-spot cards, such as “5 more minutes” and “what we do next.” There is a rules poster and a three-page Family Play & Screen Plan. A 30-day tracker holds 30 plays that need nothing to buy. Each has a starting age, easier and harder ways and a 2-minute version. A certificate marks the end.

Tokens are for play and time together, never screen minutes. The screen spot stays the same every day. A two-page grown-up guide covers a 2-minute setup, three talk lines and how it works from 2 to 5, plus printing, laminating and velcro tips. Every play follows our published safety rules.

You get color and low-ink files in US Letter and A4, with type-in fields for free Adobe Acrobat Reader. Instant download; nothing ships.

  • 9 printable tools, 41 pages (color file) = 16 checklist pages + 12 tool pages + 3 family-plan pages + 3 play-guide pages + certificate + 5 guide pages + 1 next-steps page; about 20 minutes to prep, then reusable

Questions

What’s inside, and do I have to use it all?

9 tools for ages 2–5 in a color file and a low-ink file, US Letter and A4. Most families use 2 or 3 of them; start with the checklist.

Does my child have to earn screen time?

No. Screens have the same spot every day, whatever happens with jobs or behavior. Together tokens are for play and time together, never screen minutes.

My child uses a talker (a device to talk). Does it count as a screen?

No. A talker is your child’s voice, so it stays with them at meals, in the car and at night. The guide and the family plan both say so.

Which ages is it for?

Ages 2–5. Big pictures for little ones, and blanks you can fill in for any age. Every one of the 30 plays shows a starting age in months. Ages are a guide, never a deadline.

Can I give it as a gift?

Yes. Buy it and forward the download email to the family, or print it for them. The personal license then belongs to that family.

Can grandparents or a sitter use it?

Yes. The personal license covers grandparents and sitters who care for your child. Take the board and tokens along; the safety notes on page 5 go with them.

Is there a Spanish version?

Not yet. You can type your own words in Spanish on the fillable pages (accents like á and ñ work), or print blank and write by hand. A Spanish edition would be made by a human translator.

Is there a printed book?

Not yet. If a printed edition is made, we will say so here.

What can I edit?

Text boxes: names, dates, jobs, rules, token ideas, screen-spot time and length, and plan answers. Colors and pictures can’t be changed. Every page also prints blank.

How does the download work?

Right after checkout you get a download link on screen and by email. The files are plain PDFs, so they open on a phone, tablet or computer. Print at “Actual size” or “100%”.

What can I do with it?

Use it with your own household, as often as you like. Please share a link to this page rather than the files. License terms

What if something is wrong?

Our shipping and returns page sets out exactly what happens if a file is broken, a book arrives damaged, or something isn’t as described.
